s: to join in approving, consent, agree to or with
5102.full: συν-ευ-δοκέω, -ῶ [in LXX: 1Ma.1:57, 1Ma.4:28 א1, 2Ma.11:24 2Mac 11:35 * ;] to join in approving, consent, agree to or with: absol., Act.22:20; with dative of person(s), Rom.1:32; with dative of thing(s), Luk.11:48, Act.8:1; with inf., 1Co.7:12-13 (chiefly in late writers).† (AS)

5104.full: συνοδία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Neh.7:5, 64 (יָחַשׂ) * ;] __1. a journey in company (Plut., al.). __2. By meton., κ company of travellers, a caravan: Luk.2:44.† (AS)

5105.full: συν-τόμως, adv. (συντέμνω) [in LXX: Pro.13:23 23:28, 3Ma.5:25 * ;] concisely, briefly: Act.24:4 (for a similar ex., see MM, xxiv).† (AS)

s: to frame with art, devise cunningly
5106.full: to weave together : metaphorically to frame with art, devise cunningly , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., ὥστε ταῦτα συνυφανθῆναι so that this web was woven , i. e. this business undertaken, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

5108.full: συν-έπομαι [in LXX: 2Ma.15:2, 3Ma.5:48 R 3Ma.6:21 * ;] to follow with, accompany: with dative of person(s), Act.20:4.† (AS)

5110.full: 1. to shade quite over, throw a shade over, shade closely or thickly , (Hesiod); γένυν ς., i. e.to get a beard, (Euripides): metaphorically, συσκηνῶσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας (Demosthenes Orator) 2. intransitive to be thick-shaded , (Euripides) (ML)

5113.full: σχέδον adv. (ἔχω), [in LXX: 2Ma.5:2, 3Ma.5:14 3Mac 5:45 * ;] __1. of place, near. __2. Of degree, almost, nearly: Act.13:44 19:26, Heb.9:22.† (AS)

5115.lxx: in LXX: Exo.5:8, 17, Psa.46:10 (רָפָה ni., hi.) *
5115.full: σχολάζω (σχολή), [in LXX: Exo.5:8, 17, Psa.46:10 (רָפָה ni., hi.) * ;] to be at leisure, hence, to have time or opportunity for, to devote oneself to, be occupied in: 1Co.7:5; of things, to be unoccupied, empty (Plut., Eur., al.): οἶκος, Mat.12:44, Luk.11:25 (T [WH], R, om.).† (AS)

s: that for which leisure is employed, a disputation, lecture
the place where lectures are delivered, a school
5116.lxx: in LXX: Gen.33:14 (κατὰ σ., אַט), Pro.28:19, Sir.38:24 *
5116.full: σχολή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: Gen.33:14 (κατὰ σ., אַט), Pro.28:19, Sir.38:24 * ;] __1. leisure. __2. Later (from Plato on), __(a) that for which leisure is employed, a disputation, lecture; __(b) the place where lectures are delivered, a school: Act.19:9 (for the later sense of employment, see MM, xxiv).† (AS)

5119.lxx: in LXX: Wis.14:20 15:17, Da TH Bel 1:27 *
5119.full: σέβασμα, -τος, τό (σεβάζομαι), [in LXX: Wis.14:20 15:17, Da TH Bel 1:27 * ;] an object of worship: Act.17:23, 2Th.2:4.† (AS)

5121.full: 1. a sign or token by which one infers a thing, [variant datesTragica Adespota; λαμπάδος τὸ σύμβολον the token of the beacon-fire, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;often in plural, of marks on the body, (Euripides); of omens , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. a pledge or pawn , on which money was advanced, (Lysias Orator) 3. in plural tallies , Lat. tesserae hospitales, i.e. the halves of a bone or coin, which two persons broke between them, each keeping one piece, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 4. at Athens, a ticket, counter , Lat. tessera, such as were given to the dicasts, on presenting which they received their fee, (Demosthenes Orator) 5. a permit or licence to reside, given to aliens , (Aristophanes Comicus); a ticket given by each person who joined in a picnic, to be presented for payment at the end (compare συμβολή IV), (Aristophanes Comicus) 6. in Eccl. the distinctive mark of Christians, a confession of faith, a creed , Lat. symbolum. 7. in legal phrase, σύμβολα were covenants between two states for protection of commerce , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; σύμβολα ποιεῖσθαι πρὸς πόλιν to make a commercial treaty with a state, τὰ ς. συγχέειν to violate such treaty , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

5122.full: σύμ-φυτος, -ον (συμφύω, to make to grow together) [in LXX: Zec.11:2 (בָּצַר), Est.7:7 Est.7:8 א2, Amo.9:13, 3Ma.3:22 * ;] __1. congenital, innate (Plat., al.; 3Mac, l.with). __2. grown along with, united with: τ. ὁμοιώματι τ. θανάτου αὐτσῦ (see Field, Notes, 155 f.), Rom.6:5.† (AS)

5124.full: closely shaded, thickly shaded , (Xenophon Historicus); σύσκιόν τι a closely-shaded place , (Lucian) (ML)

s: a sure sign, a positive proof
5125.full: τεκμήριον, -ου, τό (τέκμαρ, a mark, sign), [in LXX: Wis.5:4 19:13, 3Ma.3:24 * ;] a sure sign, a positive proof: Act.1:1-26 (for exx., see MM, xxiv).† SYN.: ἔνδειγμα, q.v (AS)

5126.full: fourteen , Lat. quatuordecim, the first part remaining unaltered with a neut. Substantive, as, τεσσερεσκαίδεκα ἔτη (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: of such an age, so old
5128.full: τηλικοῦτος, -αύτη, -οῦτο (altern. of τηλικόσδε, -ήδε, -όνδε, strength­ened form of τηλίκος), [in LXX: 2Ma.12:3, 3Ma.3:9, 4Ma.16:4 * ;] __1. of persons, __(a) of such an age, so old; __(b) so young. __2. Of things, so great: 2Co.1:10, Heb.2:3, Jas.3:4, Rev.16:18.† (AS)

5136.full: τροφο-φορέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Deu.1:31 (נָשָׂא), 2Ma.7:27 * ;] to nourish (Hesych.), bear like a nurse (R, mg., bare he them as a nursing-father): with accusative of person(s), Act.13:18, T, Tr., R, mg. (WH, R, txt., τροποφορέω, which see).† (AS)

5137.full: enjoyment, delight , τινός from or in a thing, (Hesiod):—;absolute gladness, joy, delight, pleasure , (Theognis Elegiacus) (ML)

5142.full: φαρμακία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ (φαρμακεύω, to administer drugs) poët. and late prose form of φαρμακεία, [in LXX: Exo.7:11, 22 8:7, 18 (3, 14) (לָט, חַרְטֹם), Isa.47:9, 12 (כֶּשֶׁף) Wis.12:4 18:13 * ;] __1. generally, the use of medicine, drugs or spells (Xen.). __2. (a) poisoning (Plut., Polyb.); __(b) sorcery, witchcraft: Gal.5:20 (see Lft., in l), Rev.9:21 (WH, txt., φαρμάκων) Rev.18:23 (cf. LXX, ll. with).† (AS)

5143.full: 1. to administer a drug , (Plato Philosophus) 2. to use enchantments , φαρμακεύειν τι ἐς τὸν ποταμόν to use it as a charm to calm the river, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. with accusative pers. to drug, give him a poisonous or stupefying drug , (Euripides) (ML)

5145.full: φθαρτός, -ή, -όν (φθείρω) [in LXX: Lev.22:25 (מִשְׁחָת), Isa.54:17 A א3, Wis.9:15 14:8, 2Ma.7:16 * ;] perishable, corruptible: ἄνθρωπος, Rom.1:23 (opposite to ἄφθαρτος θεός); στέφανος, 1Co.9:25 (opposite to αρτος); σπσρά, 1Pe.1:23 (opposite to ἄφθ.); neut., τὸ φ. τοῦτο, 1Co.15:53-54; pl., 1Pe.1:18.† (AS)

s: the love of brothers, brotherly love
5146.full: φιλαδελφία, -ας, ἡ (φιλάδελφος), [in LXX: 4Ma.13:23 4Mac 13:26 4Mac 14:1 * ;] the love of brothers, brotherly love: of Christians' mutual love as brethren (see: ἀδελφός), Rom.12:10, 1Th.4:9, Heb.13:1, 1Pe.1:22, 2Pe.1:7.† (AS)

5148.full: φιλονεικία, -ας, ἡ (φιλόνεικος), [in LXX: 2Ma.4:4, 4Ma.1:26 4Mac 8:26 * ;] love of strife, rivalry, emulation (Plat., al.), but mostly in bad sense (Thuc., al.), contentiousness, contention: Luk.22:24 (but see Field, Notes, 75 f.).† (AS)

5150.full: φιλό-σοφος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Dan LXX 1:20 (אַשָּׁף), 4Ma.1:1 4Mac 5:35 4Mac 7:7 * ;] a philosopher: Act.17:18.† (AS)

5151.full: φιλότεκνος, -ον (φίλος, τέκνον), [in LXX: 4Ma.15:4-6 * ;] loving one's children (Hdt., Arist., Plut., al.): of women, joined with φίλανδρος, which see, Tit.2:4.† (AS)

5152.full: 1. a muzzle , Lat. capistrum, (Lucian) 2. the nose-band of a horse's bridle, fitted with pipes through which the horses' breath made a whistling sound, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. a kind of cup , used as a dice-box , Lat. fritillus, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

5154.full: 1. to mix flour or meal so as to make it into dough, to knead , (Herdotus Historicus); γῆν φυράσειν φόνῳ to make earth into a bloody paste , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., οἴνῳ καὶ ἐλαίῳ πεφυραμένα ἄλφιτα (Thucydides) 2. metaphorically, μαλακὴν φωνὴν φυράσασθαι to make up a soft voice, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

5155.full: φυτεία, -ας, ἡ (φυτεύω), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:29 (נָטַע), Mic.1:6, Eze.17:7 (מַטָּע) * ;] __1. a planting (Xen., al.; LXX). __2. = φύτευμα, that which is planted, a plant (Inscr.): Mat.15:13.† (AS)

5156.full: φάρμακον, -ου, τό, [in LXX for כֶּשֶׁף ;] __(a) a drug; __(b) an in­cantation, enchantment: Rev.9:21, Tr., mg., WH, txt. (RV, sorceries).† (AS)

s: that which is mixed or kneaded, a lump
5157.lxx: in LXX: Exo.8:3 (Exo.7:28) Exo.12:34 (מִשְׁאֶרֶת), מִשְׁאֶרֶת), Num.15:20-21 (עֲרִיסָה) *
5157.full: φύραμα, -τος, τό (φυράω, to mix), [in LXX: Exo.8:3 (Exo.7:28) Exo.12:34 (מִשְׁאֶרֶת), מִשְׁאֶרֶת), Num.15:20-21 (עֲרִיסָה) * ;] that which is mixed or kneaded, a lump: of dough, Rom.11:16, 1Co.5:6-7, Gal.5:9; of clay, Rom.9:21.† (AS)

5159.full: χαρακτήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ (χαράσσω, to engrave), [in LXX: Lev.13:28 (צָרֶבֶת), 2Ma.4:10, 4Ma.15:4 א R * ;] __1. a tool for graving. __2. a stamp or impress: as on a coin or seal; metaphorically, χ. τ. ὑποστάσεως, Heb.1:3.† (AS)

s: the frog in a horse's foot
5160.full: 1. the swallow , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; the twittering of the swallow was proverbially used of barbarous tongues by the Greeks, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χελιδόνων μουσεῖα (see. μουσεῖον); proverbs also, μία χελιδὼν ἔαρ οὐ ποιεῖ (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. the frog in a horse's foot , so called from its being forked like the swallow's tail , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

s: to be bereaved of a husband, to be widowed, live in widowhood
5163.full: 1. intransitive to be bereaved of a person or thing, with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. absolute to be bereaved of a husband, to be widowed, live in widowhood , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.;—;of a man, to be a widower , (Plutarch); so, χηρεύσει λέχος (Euripides) 3. to live in solitude , of an exile, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. transitive to bereave , (Euripides) (ML)

5164.full: χλευάζω (χλεύη, a jest), [in LXX: Wis.11:14, 2Ma.7:7, 4Ma.5:22 * ;] to jest, mock, jeer: Act.17:32.† (AS)

s: a chænix, a dry measure of rather less than a quart
5166.full: χοῖνιξ, -ικος, ἡ [in LXX: Eze.45:10-11 (בַּת) * ;] a chænix, a dry measure of rather less than a quart: Rev.6:6 (EV, measure).† (AS)

5167.full: to neigh, whinny , Lat. hinnire, of horses, (Iliad by Homer), etc. Formed from the sound. (ML)

5168.full: χρηματισμός, -οῦ), ὁ (χρηματίζω, which see), [in LXX: Pro.31:1 (מַשָּׂא), 2Ma.2:4 2Mac 11:17 * ;] a divine response, an oracle: Rom.11:4 (Xen., Plat., al.).† (AS)

s: the colour of the skin, the complexion
5169.full: 1. the surface of a body, the skin; the body itself, (Iliad by Homer) 2. the superficial appearance of a thing, its colour , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;especially the colour of the skin, the complexion , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

5170.full: χρυσό-λιθος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Exo.28:20 36:20 (Exo.39:13), Eze.28:13 (תַּרְשִׁישׁ) * ;] a chrysolite (on its identification, see Swete, Ap., 288 f.; DB, iv, 620): Rev.21:20.† (AS)

5172.full: of copper or bronze, brasen , (Homer); χαλκήιος δόμος, = χαλκεῖον, a forge , (Odyssey by Homer); χάλκειον γένος, of the Age of brass , (Hesiod) (ML)

5173.full: 1. a she-goat , Lat. capra, (Iliad by Homer), attic 2. Χίμαιρα, ἡ, Chimaera , a firespouting-monster, with lion's head, serpent's tail, and goat's body, killed by Bellerophon, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

5174.full: 1. like χόλη, gall, bile , (Iliad by Homer) 2. generally metaphorically bile, gall, bitter anger, wrath , (Homer), attic; χόλος ἔδυ τινά (Iliad by Homer); χόλος ἔμπεσε θυμῷ (Iliad by Homer); χόλον πέσσειν, καταπέσσειν (see. entry); χ. σβέσσαι παῦσαι (Iliad by Homer); χόλου παύεσθαι (Hesiod):—;with genitive objecti, anger towards or because of another, (Iliad by Homer); with genitive rei, anger for, because of a thing, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. an object of anger , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

5176.full: like a starling , i. e. speckled, dappled , ψ. ἵππος a dapple-gray horse, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

5177.lxx: in LXX: Exo.20:16, Deu.5:20 (17) (עָנָה), Da TH Su 1:61 AB2R (see ψευδομάρτυς) *
5177.full: ψευδο-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Exo.20:16, Deu.5:20 (17) (עָנָה), Da TH Su 1:61 AB2R (see ψευδομάρτυς) * ;] to bear false witness: Mat.19:18, Mrk.10:19, Luk.18:20" (LXX) ; before κατά, with genitive of person(s), Mrk.14:56-57 (Xen., Plat., al.).† (AS)

5179.full: to whisper, say into the ear , (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically, ὅταν πλάτανος πτελέᾳ ψιθυρίζῃ when the plane whispers to the elm, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

5180.full: ψυχικός, -ή, -όν (ψυχή) [in LXX: 4Ma.1:32 * ;] of the ψυχή (as the lower part of the immaterial in man), EV, natural: opposite to πνευματικός, 1Co.2:14 15:44 15:46; πνεῦμα μὴ ἔχοντες (EV, sensual; R, mg., natural or animal; better perhaps, of the mind; see infr.), Ju 19; with ἐπίγειος, δαιμονιώδης, opposite to ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη (σοψία), of the mind (Hort, in l), Jas.3:15† (AS)

5181.full: ψυχρός, -ά, -όν (ψύχω), [in LXX: Pro.25:25 (קַר), Sir.43:20, 4Ma.11:26 * ;] cold: sc. ὕδωρ (cf. Theogn., 263; Hdt., ii, 37), Mat.10:42; metaphorically, of indifferent persons, Rev.3:15-16 † (AS)

5182.full: the itch, scurvy, scab, mange , Lat. scabies, impetigo, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

5186.full: ἀγνωσία, -ας, ἡ (γινώσκω), [in LXX: Job.35:16 (בִּבְלִי־דַּעַת), Wis.13:1, 3Ma.5:27 * ;] ignorance (opposite to γνῶσις): 1Co.15:34, 1Pe.2:15 (see Hort in l.; MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

5187.full: ἀγωνία, -ας, ἡ (ἀγών), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:14,16 15:19 * ;] __1. a contest, wrestling (Eur., Xen.). __2. Of the mind, great fear, agony, anguish (Dem., Arist.): Luk.22:44 (cf . Field, Notes, 77 f. ; Abbott, Essays, 101 f. ; MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

5190.full: not-working, idle , (Homer), etc.;—; ἀεργοὶ δόμοι idle houses, i. e. where people are idle , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)—;Cf. attic ἀργός. (ML)

5192.full: want of heart, faintheartedness , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; εἰς ἀθυμίαν καθιστάναι τινά (Plato Philosophus); ἀθυμίαν παρέχειν τινί (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν ἀθυμίαι εἶναι (Xenophon Historicus); ἀθυμία ἐμπίπτει τινί (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

5196.full: ἀκριβῶς adv. (ἀκριβής), [in LXX: Deu.19:18 (יָטַב), Da TH 7:19 (יְצֵב), Eze.39:14, Wis.19:18, Sir.18:29 ;] with exactness, carefully: Mat.2:8, Luk.1:3, Act.18:25, Eph.5:15, 1Th.5:2 (M, Th., in l). Compar., ἀκριβέστερον (Milligan, NTD, 111; MM, VGT, see word), Act.18:26 23:15, 20 24:22.† (AS)

s: the extremities of the body, hands and feet, fingers and toes
5197.full: 1. any prominent part , ἀκρ. τοῦ οὔρεος a mountain- peak , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a cape, promontory , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. the extremity of anything, ἀκρ. νηός a ship's beak , (Herdotus Historicus) 4. in plural the extremities of the body, hands and feet, fingers and toes , (Thucydides), etc.; τὰ ἀκρ. τῆς Νίκης her wings , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

5199.full: 1. unmoved, motionless , of Delos, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus); ἐξ ἀκινήτου ποδός without stirring a step, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. idle, sluggish , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. unmoved, unaltered , of laws, (Thucydides), etc. 4. immovable, hard to move , (Plato Philosophus):—;adverb, ἀκινήτως ἔχειν to be immovable , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 5. not to be stirred or touched, inviolate , Lat. non movendus, τάφος (Herdotus Historicus): proverbial of sacred things, κινεῖν τὰ ἀκίνητα (Herdotus Historicus); also τἀκίνητα φράσαι (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. of persons, not to be shaken, steadfast, stubborn , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)
